proof.claim:
Over a sustained window, etcd's backend must not be on a one-way trip to the
quota.

WHY THIS EXISTS. The soak suite had three scenarios and not one of them waited
for anything — every assertion was evaluated within seconds of the previous
one. A suite that samples an instant cannot observe a trend, and the failure
that took the cluster down on 2026-08-16 is purely a trend:

    measured growth    ~55 MB/hour
    live working set   1.7 MB
    default quota      2 GiB
    time to NOSPACE    ~39 hours

Nothing about that is visible in a snapshot. At any single moment the backend
looks fine, right up until the moment it is 99% full and etcd goes read-only.
The cluster had been up 46 hours.

WHAT THIS PINS. Sample the backend across a real window and require that the
cluster is either not growing meaningfully, or is growing slowly enough that
reclamation keeps ahead of it. Both are acceptable outcomes; a steady climb
with nothing reclaiming is not.

It also requires that the maintenance loop is present AND has evidence of
working, because "not growing" is only reassuring if something is actually
giving space back. A cluster idle enough not to grow tells you nothing about
what happens when it is busy.

HONEST LIMITS. Twenty minutes cannot prove a 39-hour outcome; it can only
catch a cluster already climbing fast enough to matter, and confirm the
mechanism that prevents the climb is alive. A true soak belongs on a
long-running cluster, and the real one is the only place that exists. Treat a
pass here as "no acute leak and the brake is connected", not as "safe for 39
hours".

authority.note: Simulation output is evidence/candidate knowledge only. Governed promotion is required before production may rely on it.
